Title: Portsmouth Eye of Hazimel Tournament report, November 2002

Messages.Author: legbiter
Messages.Body:
Portsmouth Eye of Hazimel Tournament report, November 2002

13 Methuselahs gathered in the function room of the Old Vic pub on
Sunday afternoon, the 10th of November, to squabble over the Eye of
Hazimel, or not, as turned out more frequently to be the case. 13 was
not bad but less than i expected thanks to the no-show of such
lightweights as Barney Bakerchamp, Jon Cooper and Pierre Rebstock.
Here's who actually turned up:

Rob "Number One" Treasure from Southampton, fielding his very sweet
Tyler abuses the Archon deck [2/3 Brujah crypt].
Michael Eichler from USAF Ramstein, playing a Lasombra Blood Depletion
deck. He has posted it under "Thoughts on the Portsmouth Eye", so
check it out - in overall effect it is kinda like a cryptic
mission/theft deck, and it's really not bad.
Garry Scarlett from Portsmouth, playing a Lazverinus rush deck.
John Keech from Portsmouth, playing a Stanislawa deck.
Jack Drever from Southampton, playing a Giovanni bash/bleed deck. Jack
is 15.
Matthew Eakins from, erm, help me Matt. He is one of my project
students, and quite coincidentally is learning to play VTES, using a
group 2/3 Ventrue deck.
Matt Stockton from Portsmouth, playing a new Tremere deck.
Paul Reid-Bowen from Bath, playing a Tzimisce deck which had more
stealth-bleed and less intercept than the average such deck, plus
Crimson Fury.
Legbiter, James McClellan, me, playing my new Malkavian
Derange/Dementia suck you dry deck, of which more below.
James Coyne, another of my project students, playing a Setite/Baali
deck.
Sam Marsh aka Jazzbeaux from Bath, playing an Assamite thaumaturgy
deck with Lucas Haan. Well, he did say he would. i never got to play
against it but apparently it was quite good.
Graham Smith from Bath, playing a Ravnos bleed/bash deck that seemed
never to have any intercept or Rush. Once he finally got into combat
we got to see what the point of the deck was - Illusions of the
Kindred, Horrid Reality, Flamethrower, Trap, Amria .... great stuff!
Michael McClellan aka Anklebiter playing a Kiasyd deck with Lasombra
spice.

We played two tables of 4 and one of five, two rounds and a final [we
said we would do three rounds in the pre-publicity, but after
discussion with the players i took it down to two so that people
wouldn't get shouted at so much by their partners]. We used the
multi-judge system and did not allow people to play twice on the five
player-table. i felt that i had a slight advantage in knowing the
broad outlines of everyone's crypt and i offered to sit the match out
on that account, but it was felt not to be such an advantage and that
i should play [i was careful to choose my deck BEFORE looking at
everyone else's, and i got Michael to verify its crypt's legality].

5. Anklebiter 1VP

Here is My Deck. In my hands this deck has never lost a game. In fact
the only time it has ever lost a game is when Barney Bakerchamp
borrowed it for the London Minicon, and the only reason it lost then
was because Barney needed to sweep/got greedy [take your pick]. Both
Barney and Rob have helped me to tweak it so thank-you, Gentlemen!

Deck name: "i'm sorry, did i break your concentration?"
Description: Brit uber-sleaze takeover/bloat deck, based on new
wording of Derange, multiple master phases, Heidelberg and Malkavian
Dementia. A similar deck has been posted to the NG, but this is not a
clone or derivative of that, just another case of Great minds thinking
Alike.

**********************

Other stuff about this tournament ....... well, the Eye of Hazimel did
make an impact - Michael Eichler used it to sweep his table in the
second heat, and Michael McClellan used it to win his VP in the final.
i wonder if this tournament had the lowest average age of any ever
held .... two teenagers out of 13 players, must be close! i'm SURE
this is the first ever father-son 1-2 in Jyhad tournament history.

As for tournament moments, in my history report i am going to mention
the following milestones on the Malkavian Road to victory:

The Madness of Arika [second heat].
Gratiano [michael M] got deranged
Passed the Derange card to Arika [Matt E]
Arika got taken over by Malkavian Dementia [Legbiter, first master]
Arika was Minion tapped to 1 [Second master, thanks to rumours of
gehenna passed while Gratiano was mad]
Arika bled her true owner for 6, thanks to Conditioning - net pool
swing of 26.

The Treachery of Legbiter [final]
In the final, Rob's Tyler had disarmed Michael E's Talley who was thus
going to torpor. Rob asked how i would vote if he Amaranth-diablerised
Talley. i said i would vote for him to live. He diablerised. i voted
that Tyler burned. This appalling lower-than-a-snake's-belly manoeuver
pretty much gave me the game, and tournament.

Thanks to White Wolf and Marshall McCrombie of Southsea Models for
uber-generous prize support, and to the Old Vic for letting us use
their function room for free; props also to Matt Stockton through whom
the venue was organised. Many thanks to all who turned up and
especially the new players, upon whom i heaped, i say positively
HEAPED the largesse of White Wolf, and i think they, and everyone, had
a good time in consequence.

Messages.Author: Andy Brown
Messages.Body:
I've probably missed something here, but can I get this clarified
by someone (Maybe yourself Rob?)

1) Tyler gets made an Archon
2) The Archon card goes to the Ash Heap, and so is not in play
3) As the card is not in play, the rush ability can be used mulitple
times as the wording of the NRA is:

New Rules - No Repeat Actions

The new base rules incorporate a variation of the No Repeat Actions
special floor rule from the V:EKN tournament rules.
Instead of restricting repeats by (a sometimes difficult to define)
type, a minion cannot

bleed twice in a turn
take a political action twice in a turn
use the same action card twice in a turn
take the action allowed by a card in *play* twice in a turn

by the new rules, with no restrictions on, for example, hunting or
equipping (assuming the minion can untap, of course).
The last item (card in play) includes any special ability the minion may
have.

...and the minion has no special ability, it is granted by the Archon
card, which is not in play.

If this is the case, I might just have to start looking at combat
all over again.

Cheers

Andy "Slytherin" Brown
VEKN Setite Ruler of Cambridge
SET awakens, watch out all non-believers
